subject.title: feat(dashboard): widget capabilities — net CSP, host tools, hardened shared sandbox

question: Should OpenClaw expose the new persisted dashboard capability model and three core Gateway RPCs as the approved long-term contract, rather than keeping dashboard widgets limited to the existing surface?
rationale: This PR creates durable core protocol, persistence, and security-boundary behavior; choosing its permanent public contract cannot safely be inferred from implementation quality alone.

options.title: Approve the core capability contract
options.body: Keep the declared, revision-bound capability model and require upgrade plus real-runtime security proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow the initial scope
options.body: Limit the first landing to the smallest approved widget capability subset and defer other host tools or RPCs behind a follow-up design decision.

options.title: Route capabilities through a plugin seam
options.body: Pause the core API expansion if dashboard-specific host tools should instead be owned by a plugin or narrower extension boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve the core capability contract
recommendation.body: Keep the declared, revision-bound capability model and require upgrade plus real-runtime security proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied commits and PR design description identify this person as the concrete proposer of the dashboard capability contract.
